title: Cross-Chain USDC Migration from Ethereum Aave to Arbitrum Aave
description: Migrate 500,000 USDC from Aave on Ethereum to Aave on Arbitrum via Hop Protocol for higher yield on Arbitrum.

mission.description: Migrate liquidity cross-chain to capture higher yields while maintaining capital efficiency and security
constraints: Only use Hop Protocol for bridging (most battle-tested cross-chain bridge)
Must repay all Aave debt before withdrawing collateral
Verify Arbitrum bridge finality before depositing on destination Aave
Maintain at least 9.8 ETH on Ethereum for future use

mission_prompt: You have 500,000 USDC supplied on Aave (Ethereum) with 50,000 USDC borrowed against it, plus 10 ETH and 50,000 USDC in wallet. Ethereum Aave USDC supply APY is 3.8%, but Arbitrum Aave offers 5.5% on USDC. Migrate the full 500k USDC from Ethereum Aave to Arbitrum Aave using Hop Protocol. You have 0.1 ETH on Arbitrum for gas. Bridge fee on Hop is ~0.05%. Your health factor is currently 8.0. First repay the 50k debt with your wallet USDC, then withdraw the full 500k, bridge via Hop, and deposit on Arbitrum Aave. Total yield gain: ~$8,500/year. Migration cost: ~$300-350. Break-even: ~15 days.

optimal_actions.action: Assess current Ethereum Aave position and compute health factor
optimal_actions.rationale: Supplied: 500,000 USDC ($500k). Borrowed: 50,000 USDC ($50k). Collateral (ETH equivalent): 500000/3000 = 166.67 ETH. Debt (ETH equivalent): 50000/3000 = 16.67 ETH. HF = (166.67 * 0.80) / 16.67 = 8.0. Verify no risk of liquidation during migration.

optimal_actions.action: Compare Ethereum vs Arbitrum Aave USDC supply APYs and compute migration benefit
optimal_actions.rationale: Ethereum: 3.8% APY. Arbitrum: 5.5% APY. Delta: +1.7 pp. Annual gain: 500000 * 0.017 = $8,500/year. Bridge cost: ~$300. Break-even: ~13 days. Migration is financially sound.

optimal_actions.action: Repay 50,000 USDC debt on Ethereum Aave using wallet USDC
optimal_actions.rationale: Must eliminate debt before withdrawing collateral. Wallet has exactly 50,000 USDC — sufficient. Post-repayment: 0 USDC wallet, 500k USDC supplied, 0 USDC debt. Gas: ~$5-10.
No remaining debt, so full withdrawal is possible. Post-withdrawal: 500,000 USDC in wallet, no Aave position on Ethereum. Gas: ~$15-25.

optimal_actions.action: Approve Hop Protocol bridge contract for USDC transfer
optimal_actions.rationale: ERC-20 approval required before Hop can transfer USDC. Approve 500,000 USDC. Gas: ~$10-15.

optimal_actions.action: Bridge 500,000 USDC via Hop Protocol from Ethereum to Arbitrum
optimal_actions.rationale: Bridge fee: 500000 * 0.0005 = $250. L1 gas: ~$45. Net received on Arbitrum: ~$499,700. Wait for canonical bridge finality (~15 min). Do NOT deposit before finality is confirmed.
Verify that the Hop bridge transaction is confirmed on Arbitrum. Check Arbitrum USDC balance reflects ~$499,700. Do not skip this step.

optimal_actions.action: Deposit received USDC on Arbitrum Aave
optimal_actions.rationale: Deposit ~$499,700 USDC on Arbitrum Aave at 5.5% APY. Annual yield: ~$27,484. L2 gas: ~$2-5.

optimal_actions.action: Verify final positions across both chains
optimal_actions.rationale: Ethereum: ~9.97 ETH remaining (paid ~0.03 ETH in total L1 gas), 0 USDC. Arbitrum: 0.1 ETH for gas, ~499,700 USDC earning 5.5% on Aave. Total yield improvement: ~$8,500/year vs prior strategy.

alternative_actions.strategy: Use Across bridge instead of Hop
alternative_actions.steps: Bridge via Across Protocol with similar fee structure (~0.04%) but potentially faster finality
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Slightly lower fee but Across has lower total value bridged and less battle-testing than Hop

alternative_actions.steps: Migrate 250k USDC to Arbitrum, leave 250k on Ethereum Aave
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Half the yield gain ($4,250/yr vs $8,500/yr) but maintains cross-chain diversification and reduces bridge risk

alternative_actions.strategy: Swap ETH for USDC on Ethereum, then migrate larger amount
alternative_actions.steps: Swap 2 ETH (~$6,000) for USDC, add to migration amount
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Increases yield on migrated amount but reduces ETH holdings below 9.8 constraint — violates mission constraint

risk_flags: Bridge risk: Hop Protocol could have a smart contract vulnerability — $250M+ in bridge TVL is a target
Arbitrum sequencer could experience downtime during bridge finality window
USDC de-pegging risk (although below 1% historical probability) would affect both source and destination positions
Arbitrum Aave USDC APY (5.5%) is utilization-dependent and could drop if more liquidity arrives on Arbitrum
L1 gas price spikes during peak hours could add $20-50 to migration cost
Repaying debt before withdrawing is mandatory — forgetting this order would cause transaction revert

mission_alignment_check.reason: Cross-chain migration captures 1.7 pp higher yield while using battle-tested protocols (Aave, Hop, Arbitrum). 2.5x max leverage respected (no new leverage introduced). 30% max drawdown constraint not impacted by yield optimization.

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim Hop bridge finality is instant — Arbitrum canonical bridge takes ~15 minutes; the agent must wait before depositing
Agent might suggest withdrawing USDC from Aave before repaying the 50k debt — impossible in Aave; debt must be zero to withdraw full collateral
Agent might claim a flash loan can repay the 50k debt — flash loans must be repaid in the same transaction, cannot be used for debt repayment
Agent might claim Arbitrum Aave has different USDC token address — native USDC on Arbitrum uses the same bridge-wrapped address; must verify
Agent might confuse Ethereum Aave USDC LTV (80%) with the liquidation threshold (85%) when computing health factor
Agent might claim the migration can be done in a single atomic transaction — cross-chain operations are inherently asynchronous
reasoning_path: Step 1: Query Ethereum Aave position from KG: Supplied 500k USDC, Borrowed 50k USDC
Step 3: Query Arbitrum Aave USDC supply APY (5.5%) from Protocol:Aave_Arbitrum KG node
Step 5: Check bridge costs from Hop Protocol KG node: 0.05% fee + ~$50 gas = ~$300
Step 6: Validate migration economics: $8,500/year gain vs $300 one-time cost, break-even in ~13 days
Step 7: Execute repayment on Ethereum Aave (repay() with 50000 USDC)
Step 8: Execute withdrawal on Ethereum Aave (withdraw() for 500000 USDC)
Step 9: Execute ERC-20 approve for Hop bridge contract
Step 10: Execute bridge via Hop's send() function
Step 11: Wait for bridge finality (~15 min), verify Arbitrum balance
Step 12: Deposit on Arbitrum Aave (supply() for received USDC amount)
Step 13: Final verification across both chains

success_criteria: All Aave debt on Ethereum repaid before any withdrawal
USDC bridged to Arbitrum via Hop Protocol
Bridge finality confirmed before depositing on Arbitrum Aave
Ethereum ETH balance >= 9.8 ETH after all transactions

expected_failure_modes: May attempt to withdraw USDC from Aave without repaying debt first — transaction will revert
May claim Hop bridge finality is instant and deposit before funds arrive on Arbitrum
May confuse Arbitrum USDC with Ethereum USDC token contract addresses
May forget to include ERC-20 approval step for Hop bridge contract
May propose using a flash loan to simplify cross-chain transfer — flash loans are single-chain only
May underestimate bridge time and report premature success
May retrieve Ethereum Aave APY instead of Arbitrum Aave APY when comparing yields
May retrieve stale Hop bridge fee data (0.03% instead of current 0.05%)
Cannot track asynchronous cross-chain state across Ethereum and Arbitrum simultaneously
May not correctly compute health factor improvement after partial debt repayment
